title: The Last Transmission

sources.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
sources.note: Dates, route, and radio log details as documented by the museum.

hook: On July 2nd, 1937, a plane took off from New Guinea. It was never seen again.

beats.text: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan left Lae, New Guinea, in a Lockheed Electra, bound for Howland Island — a strip of land two and a half thousand miles away.
beats.visualHint: A twin-engine 1930s aircraft on a remote Pacific airstrip at dawn, seen from a distance, haze over the runway

beats.text: Near Howland, the Coast Guard cutter Itasca waited to guide them in by radio.
beats.visualHint: A 1930s coast guard cutter alone on a vast, flat ocean under an overcast sky, wide shot

beats.text: At 7:42 in the morning, her voice came through: we must be on you, but cannot see you. Gas is running low.
beats.visualHint: Interior of a period ship radio room, a lone operator silhouetted against dim equipment lights

beats.text: Around an hour later, one final transmission. Then nothing.
beats.visualHint: Empty ocean horizon from the air, clouds, no land in sight, cold light

beats.text: The Navy and Coast Guard searched for weeks. No plane, no wreckage, no answer was ever found.
beats.visualHint: Search ships spread across open water at dusk, seen from high above, tiny against the sea

outro: The Electra, Earhart, and Noonan were declared lost at sea. What happened in that final hour is still unknown.
